findings.title: The final deniability game excludes dependence of the real record on the decoy opening
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Blocks the unqualified claim that the full deniability experiment of the text is formalized; an explicitly narrower theorem can still be published.
findings.reproduction: Inspect realRecords' type and draw order. It receives genuine P/E/tables and is sampled before the disclosed usage record. For a fixed genuine context with distinct phrases, let U be a fresh fair Boolean and let the broader real-record rule copy the realized U record.
findings.expected: The text permits the real wallet to be used in any way. The source-faithful final game can therefore sample a genuine record conditional on the realized decoy Q/state/record, as EasyCrypt dReal does.
findings.observed: The final Lean kernel supplies none of those realized decoy arguments. Its real record is conditionally independent of fresh U; the two Boolean records agree with probability 1/2, versus 1 for the allowed copy rule. The averaged theorem does not remove this restriction: usage is fixed outside Setup.
findings.impact: A concrete experimental family allowed by the text is outside the checked final Lean theorem. This is not a counterexample to its numerical advantage bound or evidence that the broader bound is false.
findings.evidence: Direct final-signature and program-body trace; independent deniability review and skeptical record-kernel challenge; exact conditional-law witness in the report.
findings.recommendedFix: Extend the accepted-branch genuine-record kernel with the decoy Q/state/realized U record, then lift existing pointwise clean-run equality and refusal composition. Alternatively publish the narrower record restriction explicitly.
findings.requiredVerification: Kernel-check an endpoint with the broader kernel and unchanged numerical bound; include a shared-record Boolean instance distinguishing the original and extended games, and preserve lookup/budget/refusal behavior.

findings.title: The documented kernel-replay loop returns success when replay fails
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Repair status propagation before advertising the command as automated kernel verification.
findings.reproduction: Substitute lake with a function that returns 7 and run the literal loop over two synthetic Lean filenames.
findings.expected: Any failed module replay makes the verifier exit nonzero and records the failed module.
findings.observed: Both FAILED messages print, but each echo succeeds and the loop returns 0.
findings.impact: Automation can report acceptance after every replay failed. The audit's separate recorder/guard preserves failures and its actual kernel results are unaffected.
findings.recommendedFix: Use a verifier with explicit nonzero aggregate status or fail immediately while preserving the actual module/code.
findings.requiredVerification: A failed stub must produce nonzero overall status; all current fresh artifacts must pass a correctly propagating loop.

findings.title: Complete-coverage wording needs the remaining domain and exact-statement qualifications
findings.affected: Publication README.md:4-6,38-41; Chapters/README.md scope; final W5/W6/W7 and ancillary result index.
findings.reproduction: Compare every numbered and rigorous unnumbered claim against its actual endpoint and inherited Fintype/totality hypotheses.
findings.expected: A literal complete-correspondence claim states restrictions and distinguishes a proved component from an assembled source-game theorem.
findings.observed: The main Theorem5 has genuine arbitrary-PMF transport, but W5/W6/W7 remain finite. Fractional attainment/lower-floor, general adaptive expected-cost source assembly, W7 bracket assembly and capped no-container inheritance have no exact exported counterpart found. Some qualifications already appear in the chapter guide.
findings.impact: Readers can infer broader or more literal formal coverage than the current endpoints establish; no wrong proved inequality follows.
findings.evidence: Per-result annexes and two independent skeptical challenges, including whole-source declaration/use searches.
findings.recommendedFix: Make scope qualifications prominent and mark the missing exact forms, or formalize them. Preserve the existing real arbitrary-PMF Theorem5 result rather than describing all of Lean as finite.
findings.requiredVerification: A correspondence table identifies matching signatures/hypotheses and labels exact, stronger, narrower and unassembled claims separately.

findings.title: The native-evaluation axiom explanation describes an older Lean mechanism
findings.reproduction: In the pinned toolchain, compile a separate true native_decide theorem, print/check its axiom closure and invoke the actual checkpoint gate.
findings.expected: The trusted-base description names the mechanism used by the pinned toolchain.
findings.observed: Lean 4.35 creates a dedicated _native...ax declaration; the README says native_decide would appear as Lean.ofReduceBool. The actual general allowlist correctly rejects the dedicated axiom as well.
findings.impact: A reader relying only on the obsolete marker could misunderstand native-proof trust. No native proof was found in the reviewed development and its gate remains effective.
findings.evidence: Pinned upstream Meta/Native.lean and official 4.35 release notes; NativeControl checkpoint rejection.
findings.recommendedFix: Describe the complete transitive axiom allowlist and version-correct native-generated axioms, without relying on one obsolete name.
findings.requiredVerification: The README agrees with the actual NativeControl axiom name and the gate still rejects all non-allowed axioms.
